articles.title: Watch: Black substance spews into the air at California landfill
articles.summary: A drilling operation at the Chiquita Canyon Landfill triggered a large release of gas and decomposing waste that neighbours are voicing concerns over.
articles.body:
A drilling operation at a landfill in Los Angeles County triggered a large release of gas and decomposing waste. Video shows a black substance spewing into the air.

The incident on Monday at Chiquita Canyon Landfill in Castaic, California, prompted an evacuation advisory, according to the Los Angeles County Fire Department.

The site has reportedly faced scrutiny since 2022 over an underground chemical reaction that has produced foul odours and fumes. California's attorney general sued the landfill's operators in late October.

articles.title: Psychology says people who read subtitles even when they understand the language may process information more comfortably when they can both hear and see it
articles.summary: You are watching a film or a web series in a language you understand perfectly well.
articles.body: You are watching a film or a web series in a language you understand perfectly well. The dialogue is clear, the actors are speaking at a normal pace and there is no obvious difficulty following the story. Yet, you still switch on subtitles. Even when someone suggests turning them off, you prefer keeping the words on the screen.You may find yourself reading every line while listening to the actors speak. Sometimes, you even notice that you miss a sentence when the subtitles disappear.For some viewers, this preference may be linked to how they process spoken information. Hearing a sentence and seeing the same words written on the screen gives them two ways to follow the conversation. Rather than depending entirely on what they hear, they can also use the written text to keep track of the dialogue.Why seeing the words can make a differenceSpoken conversations move quickly. Unlike a book, where you can pause and return to an earlier sentence, dialogue in a film continues whether or not you have caught every word. An actor may speak softly, use an unfamiliar accent, deliver several lines rapidly or speak while background music is playing. Even when viewers understand the language, they may occasionally miss a word or a part of a sentence.Subtitles provide a written version of the dialogue that viewers can follow at their own pace. They can confirm what they heard, notice a word they might have missed and understand the exact phrasing of a sentence.This involves two sources of information: the sound of the spoken words and their written form. Both can contribute to understanding the conversation, although viewers differ in how much attention they give to each.A 2026 study examined this process among Hindi-speaking bilinguals with an English-medium education background. Researchers used eye-tracking technology to examine how participants watched instructional videos under different audio and subtitle combinations.The participants watched videos with English audio and English subtitles, Hindi audio and Hindi subtitles, and English audio with Hindi subtitles. When both the audio and subtitles were in English, viewers distributed their attention between the speakers' faces and the written dialogue. When Hindi subtitles were used, they spent more time looking at the speakers' faces than reading the text.Interestingly, comprehension scores did not differ significantly between the three conditions. The researchers concluded that the language and script of subtitles influenced how viewers engaged with the written information, even when subtitles were available.The findings show that viewers do not automatically process subtitles in the same way. Their attention depends partly on how useful the written words are to them.What research says about hearing and reading at the same timeA separate 2024 study looked at how people process subtitles when watching videos with and without sound. Researchers studied 168 participants, including native English speakers from Britain and Australia and Polish speakers who used English as a second language. All participants watched English-language videos with English subtitles, once with sound and once without it. The researchers measured comprehension, recall, mental effort and eye movements.They found that participants experienced greater mental effort and lower comprehension when watching the videos without sound. When sound was available, viewers could use both the spoken dialogue and the written subtitles. The researchers also observed differences in how viewers directed their attention between the subtitles and the images.The study suggests that having access to both sound and written dialogue can support the viewing experience. However, it did not establish that everyone understands information better when subtitles are switched on.It does not necessarily mean you have difficulty listeningPeople who prefer subtitles may have different reasons for doing so. Some want to catch every word, while others find it easier to concentrate when the dialogue is also visible. For some, subtitles are simply a viewing preference developed over years of watching films and online videos.The habit also does not automatically indicate poor listening skills, difficulty understanding a language or a particular personality type. There is a difference between needing subtitles to understand a conversation and enjoying the additional support they provide. Someone may understand English comfortably in everyday conversations but still prefer reading the dialogue while watching an English-language film.The next time you switch on subtitles for a film in a language you already understand, it may not be because you failed to hear the words. You may simply prefer having the conversation in front of your eyes as well as in your ears.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ testGet the latest Lifestyle News and more. articles.title: 'ASI’s body burnt in car': Woman constable held for killing her colleague-lover
articles.summary: Woman head constable and three accomplices arrested for allegedly killing her ASI lover in Sabarkantha; body found burnt in his Maruti Ertiga near Aravali.
articles.body: PALANPUR: An assistant sub-inspector attached to Chithoda police station in Sabarkantha was allegedly murdered by a woman head constable posted at the same station — with whom he was in a relationship — because she wanted to end it.The woman head constable, Alfa Kalasva (37), and her three accomplices have been arrested for the murder of assistant sub-inspector Ashwin Tabiyad and setting his body and car on fire to destroy evidence.The case was cracked by the Aravali local crime branch (LCB) after an investigation that over several days.Tabiyad (45), a resident of Zinjhodi village in Bhiloda taluka of Aravali district, was serving as personal writer to the inspector at Chithoda police station. His charred skeletal remains were found inside his burnt Maruti Ertiga near Hathmati river on the outskirts of Padra village in Bhiloda taluka on Nov 10.He had left home in his car around 10.15pm on Nov 8 to report for duty, but never returned. His father, Babu Tabiyad, suspected the remains were those of his son.Investigators found that Tabiyad was in a relationship with Alfa Kalasva (37), a woman head constable posted at Chithoda police station and a member of its women’s safety team. They learnt that Kalasva wanted to end the relationship, while Tabiyad was pressing her to continue it. On the night of Nov 8, she allegedly called him to her rented house in Chithoda, where he stayed overnight.According to police, Kalasva killed him during the night. The next morning, she called her brother, Kalpesh Kalasva (36), who arrived with their cousin, Pankaj (28), in a Maruti Eeco. The trio allegedly placed the body in a sack and kept it inside the house through the day, said Manoharsinh Jadeja, SP, Aravali.Pankaj then drove the victim’s Ertiga to a forested area near a temple on the outskirts of Kanadar village, while Alfa and Kalpesh followed in the Eeco. They returned to Chithoda, leaving the Ertiga there.After nightfall, Kalpesh called his friend, Manoj Ninama (33). Police said the four took the body in the Eeco to the Ertiga and placed the sack inside the vehicle near the middle seat.Manoj allegedly drove the Ertiga towards Padra village while Alfa and Kalpesh followed in the Eeco. Near the Hathmati river, they poured petrol over the vehicle and set it ablaze.Investigators traced the accused through technical analysis, CCTV footage collected from locations across Aravali and Sabarkantha districts, and information from informants. Police also found that the Eeco had been used to buy petrol in a can from a fuel station in Vijaynagar before the Ertiga was set on fire. articles.title: Former London Tory MP Sir David Evennett dies after illness
articles.summary: Sir David Evennett was a Conservative MP in south-east London for more than 30 years.
articles.body:
Sir David Evennett, who served as a Conservative MP in south-east London for more than 30 years, has died aged 77 after a short illness.

He was first elected as MP for Erith and Crayford in 1983 but lost his seat in 1997. In 2005 he was elected as the MP for Bexleyheath and Crayford, a position he held until he decided not to run in the 2024 general election.

Sir David served as a Tory whip in opposition and in government, and was a vice-chairman of the party. He started his career as a teacher, and then became a councillor for Redbridge in east London.

Conservative Party chairman Kevin Hollinrake said Sir David was a "diligent" MP and "true champion of Conservatism".

Hollinrake added: "Even once he left the House of Commons, he was still a regular attendee at Kemi's (Kemi Badenoch's) speeches and an assiduous local campaigner.

Sir David also worked as a marine insurance broker at Lloyds and a lecturer in management for Bexley College.

He is survived by his wife Marilyn and his two sons.

articles.title: Apple News promoted news from left-leaning outlets 71% of time, yearlong MRC study finds
articles.summary: The Media Research Center says Apple News promoted about 60 times more stories from left-leaning outlets than right-leaning ones over a full year.
articles.body: FIRST ON FOX — The Media Research Center (MRC) has completed its first year collecting data on a trio of news apps and says it found bias against conservatives, with Apple News leading the way. The right-leaning MRC, which describes itself as an "unrelenting counterforce to leftist bias in America’s newsrooms, broadcast networks, and Big Tech platforms," examined Apple News, Google News and Microsoft’s MSN over the past 12 months. According to the MRC, all three news aggregators favored left-leaning outlets over centrist and right-leaning outlets, with Apple News showing the greatest disparity. "MRC tracked every top story Apple News, Google News and Microsoft’s MSN promoted for a full year, and the record is damning," MRC President David Bozell told Fox News Digital. APPLE, GOOGLE NEWS ALGORITHMS SUPPRESSED NEGATIVE STORIES ON MICHIGAN SENATE HOPEFUL EL-SAYED, STUDY SAYS Over the 12-month period, Apple News, which comes preinstalled on every iPhone in America, promoted about 60 times more stories from left-leaning outlets than from right-leaning outlets, according to the MRC. The findings come despite a warning the Federal Trade Commission issued to Apple on Feb. 11 over allegations of political bias in its news app. The MRC found that 71% of the 6,849 stories promoted by Apple News came from outlets rated liberal by AllSides, which rates news outlets for political bias. Only 81 articles, or about 1%, came from outlets that AllSides considers right-leaning, according to the study. Google News fared slightly better in the MRC's analysis, sharing only 239 stories (roughly 4%) from right-leaning outlets out of 6,317 stories from outlets rated by AllSides, according to the MRC. Microsoft’s MSN featured a higher percentage of stories from right-leaning outlets (13%) but promoted roughly four times as many stories from left-leaning outlets (53%), according to the study. APPLE AND GOOGLE SUPPRESSED NEGATIVE GRAHAM PLATNER STORIES FOR MONTHS ON THEIR NEWS PLATFORM, STUDY FINDS "We are putting Apple, Google and Microsoft on notice. Open your curation to public scrutiny, explain how stories get chosen, and give conservative outlets a fair shot at the front page. Right now, you are showing readers a sales pitch for the left. MRC will keep exposing it, story by story, until you fix it," Bozell told Fox News Digital. Apple News has long faced accusations of liberal bias, and Fox News Digital reported earlier this year that many of the company’s top executives and board members have made substantial contributions to Democrats in various election cycles. Apple News and Microsoft did not immediately respond to a request for comment. A Google spokesperson said Google News is not a single static page that’s the same for everyone, noting that results are selected automatically by Google's systems rather than editors. The company said the MRC methodology is "flawed" because it ignores that Google News automatically updates throughout the day and shows news personalized to users' interests and locations. articles.title: GTA 6: My wife and daughter have signed a "do not disturb" contract
articles.summary: Painter and decorator Sean Little has booked the week off work to play the new Grand Theft Auto game.
articles.body:
For Grand Theft Auto superfan Sean Little, a week off work to play the latest version of the blockbuster video game wasn't enough.

He knew that if he was spending seven days at home in Dumfries and Galloway, he would be expected to walk the dogs and pull his weight in the kitchen.

So the self-employed painter and decorator persuaded his wife and daughter to sign a "non-interference contract" giving him a week off Dad duties.

For a "signing fee", they have agreed to allow him to take over their living room and play GTA6 in peace.

GTA 6 - all you need to know about Rockstar's blockbuster game

"We're not allowed to ask him to do any sort of household chores," his wife Natalie told BBC Scotland News.

"We're not allowed to make any comments of how long he's been playing it for, any comments about him being lazy because he's not moved off the couch for hours.

"He gave me some extra housekeeping money so that I can buy sort of snacky food... he won't be cooking any meals.

"Literally he will be in here playing it and that's all he's going to do."

Sean is leaving nothing to chance. He's even bought paper plates so he's not asked to wash any dishes.

He says he pulled together the contract for his wife and 13-year-old daughter, Charlotte, as a joke and filmed it for his TikTok account.

If they stick to their side of the deal it will ensure Natalie and Charlotte don't interrupt him, reveal spoilers or "set unnecessary household tasks".

And it outlines a series of banned phrases, which include:

In return, there are financial incentives for Sean's family - he's paid £50 to Natalie and £20 to Charlotte, and increased his weekly contribution to family finances to £500.

"Probably people think I'm daft, but I mean, I don't know if they're even wrong, I don't even question them, and to be honest with you, I don't care," said Sean who lives with his family in Newton Stewart.

"I don't care what people think. My family are happy, I'm happy - as long as my bubble are happy, then who cares what anybody else thinks?"

He played the first Grand Theft Auto game when he was a teenager and has been a devoted fan ever since.

He compares himself to a Star Wars fan who watched the first film when it was released in the 1970s.

"If a new Star Wars film comes out in 2026, because they're 60 years old, they don't automatically stop being a Star Wars fan," he said.

"You don't grow out of being a fan of something."

Sean was in his mid-20s when GTA 5 came out and has been waiting 13 years for the new release.

"I've been excited for it for years, probably since finishing Grand Theft Auto 5 to be honest with you," the 38-year-old said.

"If it continues with the same kind of timeline, I'll be 51 when GTA 7 comes out - still a teenager at heart probably."

Sean has been working weekends, putting in 13-hour days and putting aside a bit of spare cash in preparation for his week off.

"I'm the same when I'm going to be having a holiday, except I'm just going to be sitting in my living room playing a game," he said.

So instead of a week off work, enjoying a holiday in somewhere like Benidorm, he'll be living the life in Vice City?

"Exactly, so much better by the way," he said. "I don't know if you've been to Benidorm but Vice, it is probably better to be honest. Sorry Benidorm."

articles.title: Haitians protest in support of El Salvador’s anti-gang troop deployment
articles.summary: El Salvador’s security minister has confirmed the troops will leave once kidnapped technicians are rescued.
articles.body:
Demonstrators have marched in several Haitian cities to show support for a deployment of troops from El Salvador, despite concerns that the outside intervention may worsen instability in the Caribbean country.

On Tuesday, hundreds of protesters rallied in the streets of cities like the capital, Port-au-Prince, bearing signs with slogans like “Down with the gangs”.

Haiti has long struggled with gang violence, but the crisis worsened around 2021, after the assassination of President Jovenel Moise. His death further weakened Haiti’s central government, and experts say gangs took advantage of the eroding public confidence to expand their influence.

The October 18 kidnapping of four Salvadoran aviation technicians near Port-au-Prince prompted El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele to respond with a military operation to Haiti.

But on Monday, El Salvador confirmed it would end its deployment of about 2,500 troops once the missing Salvadoran airmen were found.

“If they reappear tomorrow, as President Bukele said, we will leave,” Salvadoran Security Minister Gustavo Villatoro said.

That announcement, however, was followed by public gestures of support and diplomatic engagements, with some top officials in Haiti encouraging the Salvadoran deployment to stay.

Haitian Justice Minister Patrick Pelissier travelled to San Salvador on Monday and expressed gratitude for the troop surge.

“The Haitian people applaud the decision of Nayib Bukele to send troops,” Pelissier said on Monday.

He added that Haitian security forces, together with their international counterparts, had recently managed to regain control of Haiti’s national football stadium, held by gangs for years.

“During the operation, we discovered several human skulls inside the stadium,” Bukele claimed in a social media post last week.

The timeline for the Salvadoran troop withdrawal is uncertain. While El Salvador has framed its deployment as a rescue mission, the leader of Haiti’s 400 Mawozo gang, Wilson Joseph, told The Associated Press that the four technicians are already dead.

Joseph added that the abduction took place in territory controlled by Chen Mechan, a rival gang. He provided no evidence to back his assertions.

Bukele, however, has championed his country’s role in confronting Haiti’s gangs, using social media to promote the offensive and sharing videos of military operations.

The Salvadoran president — who once referred to himself as the “world’s coolest dictator” — has been credited with popularising a “mano dura” or “strong hand” approach to regional security.

Faced with one of the highest homicide rates in the world, Bukele launched a hardline security crackdown on gangs in El Salvador in 2022, including mass arrests and mass trials.

His heavy-handed approach has led to a sharp decline in crime but has also been widely condemned for human rights abuses.

Critics have warned that transplanting such tactics to Haiti could spark a backlash, leading to greater instability and risks to civilians.

They have also criticised the lack of long-term planning for El Salvador’s troop deployment; a sudden withdrawal, for instance, could worsen the situation for Haiti’s security forces.

Bukele is campaigning for a third term in El Salvador’s February presidential election, and analysts speculate his actions in Haiti could be used as a campaign tool to drum up support.

The Salvadoran deployment is the latest in a series of international interventions in Haiti.

Such foreign involvement is often controversial. The United States, for instance, has sent troops to Haiti on multiple occasions in the 20th century, occupying the country for decades and seizing control of its central bank.

More recently, a United Nations-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF) arrived in Haiti in April, to help address the widespread gang violence.

Gangs control more than 80 percent of the capital region. The conflict has killed more than 22,000 people since 2022. UN reports attribute more than half of the deaths in the first nine months of the year to security operations, including the deaths of 300 civilians.

The UN also says almost 2,000 people have been displaced since the arrival of Salvadoran troops.

But Pelissier said Haiti’s government had not reported any civilian casualties in the latest operations, which he described as professional.

“The best to do is to avoid, as much as possible, human rights violations, and that’s what we are doing together,” the minister said.

articles.title: Biden addresses infamous 'we beat Medicare' debate moment in new memoir
articles.summary: Joe Biden's memoir "Promise Me, America" revisits his "we beat Medicare" 2024 debate blunder, arguing polling never showed the performance was fatal.
articles.body: Former President Joe Biden reflected on his "we beat Medicare" moment from the June 2024 debate in his new memoir, "Promise Me, America," released Tuesday. He lamented that the moment had become "Exhibit A" that he was "too old to do the job." "One moment was particularly damaging. As I was finishing an answer on the deficit, I lost my train of thought, saw that my time was running out on the clock, and rushed the final part of my answer by blurting out: 'We finally beat Medicare.' What I meant to say was, 'We finally beat Big Pharma,'" he wrote. "This had been a huge accomplishment in my administration. As part of the Inflation Reduction Act, we had secured for Medicare the power to negotiate for lower drug prices." "Ironically, this historic achievement wouldn't lift my candidacy. It would help to sink it," he continued. "What should have been a highlight of the debate became Exhibit A that I was too old to do the job." JOE BIDEN SAYS CANCER SLOWED HIM DOWN, LIMITING MEMOIR PROMOTION TOUR Biden accused President Donald Trump of repeatedly lying during the debate, writing, "Yet none of what he said would generate any impression that lasted past debate night. It would be my answers and my performance that would dominate the press coverage and political conversation in the weeks ahead." "I knew the debate had gone badly. But I knew that debates had gone badly for lots of incumbent presidents," he wrote. "Especially their first ones. I left the stage thinking I would be debating Trump once more before the election was over." Biden said pundits and Democratic leaders decided the performance was "fatal," but he argued polling immediately after the debate showed the gap between him and Trump shrinking. "It would take weeks of hammering in the press before the polls started to move downward," he wrote. "By comparison, in the days after losing his first debate with Mitt Romney, Barack had lost five points in the horse race. But the data wasn't the point. The narrative was. And the narrative was bad. There was a consensus that I had lost. Worse than that, there was a consensus that it couldn't be fixed." Biden argued that other incumbent presidents had also performed poorly in debates but later recovered. During the 2012 election cycle, Biden wrote, his debate against Mitt Romney's running mate, Paul Ryan, took on a "special urgency" after former President Barack Obama's "terrible" debate against the Republican nominee. JILL BIDEN REVEALS JOE WHISPERED 'I REALLY F---ED UP' AFTER DISASTROUS DEBATE WITH TRUMP "What happened to Barack was not unique. Presidents seeking reelection often have terrible first debates that create media firestorms," Biden wrote. "Ronald Reagan looked lost and confused against Walter Mondale, which is why his quip at their next debate that he wouldn't answer questions about his age because he didn't want to exploit his opponent's 'youth and inexperience' was so effective." "George W. Bush was caught with a scowling face," he continued. "Barack looked like he didn't care if he won or lost. There's a reason most incumbent presidents have a bad first debate: They're more focused on the country's and the world's problems than on campaigning. Running the country is the most demanding job in the world — and running for reelection means a second job on top of that." "The difference in 2024 was not that I had a bad debate," Biden said. "Lots of presidents had bad debates. The difference was that every other president was given the chance to redeem themselves in a second debate. As it turned out, that chance would not be available to me." BIDEN ACCUSES PELOSI OF WORKING 'FURIOUSLY' BEHIND SCENES TO DERAIL HIS 2024 CAMPAIGN In an interview about his memoir, Biden said he considered his debate performance inconsequential. "Look, I don’t know anybody who hasn’t made a mistake in a debate," Biden told People magazine. "To me, it was not very consequential. First of all, I thought there’d be another debate, which there wasn’t." Biden wrote that the debate "didn't feel right from the start," before describing the moment he believed helped end his candidacy. The debate ultimately preceded his decision to exit the race after weeks of pressure from fellow Democrats. Former first lady Jill Biden said during a CBS News "Sunday Morning" interview in May that she thought her husband was having a stroke on stage during the debate. "Biden is correct. He was not the only president to have a bad debate performance," Costas Panagopoulos, professor of political science at Northeastern University, told Fox News Digital about Biden's remarks. "Previous candidates did have an opportunity to recover. The problem for Biden was not simply that he had a bad debate but rather that his poor performance reinforced a prevalent narrative that he was ill-equipped to run the country given his advanced age." articles.title: An Indiana farm drone allegedly lost control and struck Lonnie Howard's arm during a 2024 crop-spraying job; on November 16, appeals judges ruled the farmer was not liable because he did not control the drone
articles.summary: A crop-spraying operation on an Indiana farm turned into a legal dispute after an agricultural drone allegedly struck Lonnie Howard on the arm, leaving
articles.body: A crop-spraying operation on an Indiana farm turned into a legal dispute after an agricultural drone allegedly struck Lonnie Howard on the arm, leaving him claiming serious injuries. The incident raised questions about who could be held responsible when equipment operated by one person causes an accident on land occupied by someone else.In a November 16, 2026, memorandum decision, available on Justia, the Indiana Court of Appeals ruled that the farmer who had arranged for the crop to be sprayed could not be held liable under the premises-liability claim because he did not control how the drone operation was carried out. The decision upheld summary judgment in favour of the farmer. The court's ruling was based on the evidence concerning his involvement in the work, rather than a finding that the drone incident had not occurred.How the drone incident happenedThe incident took place on August 19, 2024, on a farm in Scott County, Indiana. Mark D Rose had leased the farmland from MMR Farms LLC, a company whose sole member was his son, Mark M Rose. The father asked his son to apply fungicide to a corn crop growing on the property. His son agreed to carry out the work without payment, and the father purchased the fungicide for him to use. The son then used an agricultural drone to spray the crop.During the operation, the drone allegedly stopped responding to its controls and struck Lonnie Howard in the arm. Howard claimed that he suffered an injury as a result. The father was not present when the spraying took place and did not supervise the operation. Howard and his wife, Lisa, subsequently brought a lawsuit involving the father, the son and MMR Farms. Their claim against the father ultimately focused on premises liability, arguing that he could be held responsible for the incident because it happened on the farm he occupied.Why the farmer was held not liableThe father sought summary judgment, arguing that he had not controlled the way his son carried out the spraying. The trial court granted his request in June 2026, finding that the evidence did not establish a basis for holding him liable. The Howards challenged that decision before the Court of Appeals. They argued that the father had sufficient control over the property and knew that his son would be using a drone. They also raised concerns about the son's experience operating the equipment.The appeals court examined the distinction between responsibility for property and control over work performed by another person. A person who possesses or occupies land may have a duty to protect visitors from certain dangers on the premises. However, that does not automatically make the person responsible for the way an independent contractor carries out a job.The judges focused on whether the father had controlled the manner or means of the fungicide application. The evidence showed that he had asked his son to spray the crop and provided the chemical needed for the task. The evidence presented did not establish that the father had directed how the drone should be operated.What the ruling means for the caseThe Court of Appeals affirmed the trial court's summary judgment in favour of Mark D Rose. This means the premises-liability claim against him could not proceed on the evidence presented. articles.title: Israel parliament elects Gadi Eisenkot ally Matan Kahana as new speaker
articles.summary: Eisenkot’s bloc has pledged to undo some of Netanyahu’s most contentious domestic policies following Kahana’s election.
articles.body:
Israeli lawmakers have elected Matan Kahana as the new parliament speaker , marking a step towards reversing domestic policies from the outgoing government led by Benjamin Netanyahu.

Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot – the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace Netanyahu – was voted in on Tuesday, receiving 66 votes in the 120-member chamber.

Netanyahu’s Likud party had put forward Ofir Katz as its own candidate. He received 52 votes following a stormy debate that stretched over seven hours.

The Israel parliament speaker is an important office given that it sets the timetable for parliamentary business and can therefore speed up or delay debates or votes on proposed legislation.

“I will be a Knesset speaker for everyone, irrespective of race, religion or gender,” said Kahana during his inauguration speech immediately after the vote.

Kahana, a 54-year-old former special forces soldier, is expected as soon as Wednesday to start the process of undoing much of Netanyahu’s domestic agenda, especially regarding contentious reforms to the judiciary.

Netanyahu is Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, having been in and out of office for three decades.

The vote took place weeks after October 27 parliamentary elections in which neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu won a majority in the Knesset, with the two blocs trading barbs since then.

Eisenkot’s wide-ranging bloc secured 48 seats, while Netanyahu’s finished with 53. Two Arab-majority slates won an unprecedented 19 seats on the back of anger over Netanyahu’s hard-right government.

On Tuesday, the two lists voted for Eisenkot’s candidate Kahana as parliament speaker, with one Arab Knesset member absent.

Netanyahu’s and Eisenkot’s parties met on Sunday to discuss the possibility of joining a unity government but the meeting appeared to be largely a formality, with both men saying they should be prime minister.

Netanyahu, who has reportedly been urging US President Donald Trump to resume the war on Iran, has talked up the threat from Tehran as he insists on the need for a unity government.

With Kahana at the helm and if Eisenkot retains the backing of the Arab-Israeli parties, he has an opportunity to deal serious blows to Netanyahu’s legislative agenda even before a possible government is formed.

Eisenkot has said he wants to rescind sweeping reforms to reduce the independence of the judiciary that were advanced by Netanyahu, who has been enraged over corruption charges against him that could land him in prison if he loses power.

Eisenkot has also vowed to quickly set up a state commission of inquiry to investigate security failures that led to Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack.

Netanyahu, who has built his brand on saying he will ensure Israel’s security, has refused an independent probe, instead proposing one whose members would be chosen by politicians.

Kahana, who is now a member of Eisenkot’s Yashar party, served in a short-lived non-Netanyahu government in 2021 and 2022 as minister for religious services, during which he clashed with ultra-Orthodox Jews by seeking to reduce the power of the Chief Rabbinate.

Kahana himself is an observant Jew, part of Eisenkot’s efforts to form a broad coalition that ranges from secular liberals to religious conservatives.

As parliament speaker, Kahana succeeds Amir Ohana, a Netanyahu ally who has held the position since 2022.

articles.title: A street outside Will Smith's former high school in Philadelphia now bears his name; the actor returned to the neighbourhood where his teacher gave him the nickname ‘The Fresh Prince’
articles.summary: Philadelphia has honoured one of its most famous hometown personalities by naming a street after actor and musician Will Smith.
articles.body: Philadelphia has honoured one of its most famous hometown personalities by naming a street after actor and musician Will Smith. The tribute took place outside Overbrook High School in West Philadelphia, where Smith spent his school years and developed the nickname that later became central to his entertainment career. Returning to the neighbourhood on 26 March 2025, the actor received a warm welcome from residents, students and city officials as they gathered to celebrate his achievements and his connection to the city.Will Smith Way recognises the actor's West Philadelphia rootsAccording to WHYY, a section of 59th Street, directly across from Overbrook High School, was officially renamed Will Smith Way during a ceremony attended by the actor, Philadelphia Mayor Cherelle Parker and other city leaders.The street naming was intended to recognise Smith's achievements in music, television and film, while also celebrating his connection to the neighbourhood where he grew up. For the actor, the occasion carried a personal meaning because Overbrook High School was not simply a location associated with his past. It was also where an important part of his public identity began to take shape.Smith attended the school during his teenage years, and the ceremony brought him back to the place where his journey towards international recognition first started.The Philadelphia City Council had formally approved the change earlier in March. According to the official legislative record, a resolution was introduced on 27 February 2025 and adopted on 6 March 2025. The proposal specifically covered the 2000 block of North 59th Street and described the renaming as a way to honour Smith's career and legacy as a West Philadelphia native.The resolution was sponsored by Councilmember Curtis Jones Jr. and received support from several other council members, including Council President Kenyatta Johnson. It recognised Smith's contribution to entertainment and his influence on global culture over a career spanning more than three decades.How did the neighbourhood shape the Fresh PrinceSmith was born in Philadelphia on 25 September 1968 and spent his formative years in the Wynnefield section of the city. The official resolution noted that growing up in a close-knit, working-class community helped shape the values and work ethic that later became important to his career.His early interest in entertainment developed during his teenage years. At Overbrook High School, Smith began exploring his creativity, eventually finding his way into music alongside his childhood friend Jeff Townes, better known as DJ Jazzy Jeff.The pair went on to form rap duo DJ Jazzy Jeff & The Fresh Prince and started to build up a following in the late 1980s. The music was an essential starting point for Smith, propelling him from a young performer in Philadelphia to a rising name in the American music business.They had their first big success in 1989, when their song "Parents Just Don't Understand" won the first Grammy Award for Best Rap Performance. It was a historic moment in hip-hop and a turning point in Smith’s rise to stardom.The school where the Fresh Prince nickname beganThe street naming ceremony also brought attention to the story behind Smith's famous stage name. During the event, the actor spoke about how a teacher at Overbrook High School helped give him the nickname that would eventually become recognised around the world.According to WHYY, Smith recalled that his 10th-grade teacher, Miss Brown, used to call him Prince Charming. He later added the word Fresh, borrowing from hip-hop slang, to create the name The Fresh Prince.The nickname became closely associated with his music career and eventually provided the identity for his television breakthrough. In 1990, Smith moved into acting with the popular sitcom The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air, in which he played a fictionalised version of himself.Although the television series was set in Los Angeles, its central character drew heavily on Smith's experiences growing up in West Philadelphia.WHYY reported that Mayor Cherelle Parker presented Smith with the first key to the city issued by her administration. School representatives asked Smith to support the institution's upcoming 100th anniversary celebrations, giving the occasion a connection to the next generation of students as well.Philadelphia looks towards celebrating its hometown talentThe street dedication also opened the door to discussions about bringing more of Philadelphia's well-known entertainers together for future celebrations.Mayor Parker invited Smith to help the city mark the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence in 2026. She suggested organising a major concert on the Benjamin Franklin Parkway featuring artists with strong connections to Philadelphia.Among the names mentioned were DJ Jazzy Jeff, The Roots, Jill Scott and Black Thought. The proposal aimed to bring together performers who had helped establish the city's reputation in music and entertainment.Smith responded by indicating that he would attend and contact some of his fellow artists. He specifically mentioned his friendship with Meek Mill and his willingness to reach out to Jill Scott. At the time of the ceremony, Smith was also preparing to release Based on a True Story, his first new album since 2005.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Kuwait reports drone attacks as Iran, US trade attacks on Qeshm and Bahrain
articles.summary: Kuwait’s military says its air defence was repelling drones as Iran and the US hit out at each other across the Gulf.
articles.body:
Kuwait’s army has said the Gulf country is under attack by drones while the United States and Iran traded blows, marking escalating tensions in the region as a peace deal remains elusive.

The military said in a statement on X on Tuesday that “any explosion sounds heard are the result of air defence systems intercepting hostile attacks”.

The US earlier carried out several attacks on Iran’s southern island of Qeshm, in the Strait of Hormuz, hours after Iran said it launched a drone attack on a US radar system in Bahrain.

“The American attack on locations on Qeshm island caused no damage to residential, commercial, or infrastructural areas,” Ahmad Nafisi, deputy governor of Iran’s southern Hormozgan province, told the official IRNA news agency on Tuesday.

He said the situation was under control and relief agencies were on full alert. IRNA reported five to six explosions on the island on Tuesday evening.

A US official told Al Jazeera the strike hit a missile launch site on Qeshm, in response to Iran’s earlier attack on a US base in Bahrain.

US Central Command said Iranian drones aimed at a US radar system at an air base in Bahrain “were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or personnel”.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it carried out a “precision operation” with drones on the US-operated radar at the Sheikh Isa air base, in response to “repeated violations of Iranian airspace by US military drones”.

Bahrain, which hosts the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet, said its air defences intercepted the attack, and blasts were heard over the capital, Manama, according to the AFP news agency.

It was the third Iranian drone attack on Bahrain in five days after a lull of several weeks. Friday’s strike was the first Iranian attack on a Gulf country since early September, AFP reported. Reuters said it came after a Bahraini court sentenced 64 people, mostly Shia clerics, to life in prison for allegedly colluding with Iran.

Kuwait’s armed forces said on Tuesday night that its air defences were responding to “hostile drone attacks” and urged the public to follow safety instructions.

It did not say where the drones came from or whether there were casualties or damage.

Iran’s armed forces said three oil tankers struck naval mines while trying to cross the strait on Tuesday. The US military says it cleared the main routes of mines.

Since the war began on February 28, Iran has tried to restrict traffic through the strait , which normally carries about a fifth of the world’s oil, insisting that ships use only routes it has authorised. The US has responded with a naval blockade of Iranian ports and has escorted tankers.

Another tanker, the Panamanian-flagged Tara Gas, was struck on Monday about seven nautical miles north of Khasab, in Oman, causing a fire in its engine room, according to the security firm Vanguard.

Vanguard and India’s ports minister initially said all 25 crew, 24 of them Indian, were safe. But the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said the vessel was hit a second time and the crew were “currently unaccounted for”. India’s ports minister later said the crew had abandoned the vessel after a second attack and that one Indian sailor was missing. Another Panamanian-flagged tanker, the On Phoenix, was hit by an unidentified projectile off Oman’s coast on Monday.

Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, and his Omani counterpart, Badr Albusaidi, discussed safeguarding shipping and diplomatic options in Muscat, Oman’s news agencies said.

A third US aircraft carrier, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, arrived in the Middle East on Monday, and US President Donald Trump is due to hold a three-way summit on Thursday in China with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, where the Iran war is on the agenda.

articles.summary: Inscrições escolares Uberlândia 2027 começam nesta quarta (18) para a rede municipal e a Cidade da Música, com cadastro online disponível até o dia 2 de dezembro.
articles.body:
Prefeitura abre inscrição para ingresso na rede municipal de ensino de Uberlândia em 2027 — Foto: Danilo Henriques/Secom/Prefeitura de Uberlândia

Serão abertas nesta quarta-feira (18), e seguem até 2 de novembro, as inscrições online para matrículas de 2027 na rede municipal de ensino de Uberlândia e também nas Organizações da Sociedade Civil (OSCs) parceiras e na escola Cidade da Música.

A Prefeitura, por meio da Secretaria Municipal de Educação (SME), informa que é preciso preencher o forumlário eletrônico no site da prefeitura e que a inscrição não garante vaga de imediato, é o primeiro passo do processo de matrícula.

Os pais e responsáveis devem ficar atentos aos prazos informados no processo de inscrição. Para a rede municipal e OSCs, há vagas disponíveis para ingresso na Educação Infantil, para crianças nascidas entre 1º de abril de 2021 e 30 de setembro de 2026, sendo do berçário até o 2º período.

No Ensino Fundamental, as vagas são para o 1º ano para as crianças nascidas até 31 de março de 2021, até o 6º ano.

Os candidatos selecionados serão anunciados no dia 15 de dezembro de 2026, também pelo site da Prefeitura e nas listas expostas nas instituições de ensino. Durante a etapa final, conta com realização de matrícula presencial e na entrega dos documentos comprobatórios entre os dias 17 e 29 de dezembro.

Para quem tem interesse em música, a Escola Municipal Cidade da Música também faz parte do cronograma e abrirá inscrições para preenchimento de vagas e formação de cadastro de reserva em vários cursos, como Musicalização Infantil I, II e III e para crianças de 4 a 8 anos, além de Teatro e Dança-Teatro para crianças a partir de 6 anos.

Também há aulas de Canto Coral, com turmas para os grupos infanto-juvenil de 6 a 16 anos e adulto acima dos 18 anos. Os instrumentos oferecidos são flauta doce, guitarra, viola caipira, violão, percussão, teclado e desenho, destinadas a candidatos nascidos até 31 de março de 2018, acima dos 9 anos de idade.

O critério de seleção para os cursos da Cidade da Música será um sorteio público, que ocorrerá no dia 9 de dezembro de 2026, às 14h, na instituição, localizada na Rua das Juritis, n° 1.315, no bairro Cidade Jardim. A Prefeitura de Uberlândia publicará no dia 15 de dezembro a lista dos contemplados, cujas matrículas serão confirmadas entre os dias 17 e 29 do mesmo mês.

articles.title: Sem 'apagão mundial', dia 17 tem nova falha nos EUA e ataque hacker | G1
articles.standfirst: Falhas e ataques em série foram registrados desde quinta-feira (12): cinco falhas envolveram sistemas de aviação, bancário ou de segurança, enquanto hackers tentaram roubar dados bancários.
articles.summary: Falhas e ataques em série foram registrados desde quinta-feira (12): cinco falhas envolveram sistemas de aviação, bancário ou de segurança, enquanto hackers tentaram roubar dados.
articles.body:
A teoria da conspiração para um "apagão mundial" nesta terça-feira (17) não se concretizou, mas a data foi marcada por novas falhas tecnológicas e um ataque hacker em série a quase 200 sites. Desde a quinta-feira (12), cinco falhas envolveram sistemas de aviação, bancário ou de segurança, enquanto hackers tentaram roubar dados bancários.

O principal problema ocorreu em sistemas de computação com o colapso de um dia no sistema aéreo dos Estados Unidos , na sexta-feira (13). Mais de 10 mil voos foram afetados ao longo de quatro horas de aeroportos fechados e aviões em solo. Depois, falhas em bancos e até ataques hackers ajudaram a disseminar o boato do apagão mundial, que não aconteceu.

Antes, posts publicados nas redes sociais alcançaram milhões de visualizações e alimentaram a teoria conspiratória. Em um vídeo no Instagram com quase 3 milhões de visualizações, um influenciador diz: "um apagão pode estar vindo, e 33 países já mandaram a população se preparar. Sem luz, sem PIX, sem cartão, sem internet".

Nas últimas semanas, as redes sociais foram inundadas por uma "teoria" que previa, sem provas ou evidências, um suposto "apagão global" de até três meses, a partir de 17 de novembro -- o que não aconteceu. Para tentar dar credibilidade à previsão, os boatos nas redes misturam notícias e acontecimentos reais, mas que não têm qualquer relação comprovada entre si.

Veja as falhas recentes na linha do tempo abaixo:

A lista de problemas tecnológicos teve início com o Microsoft, na quinta-feira, quando uma série de aplicativos e programas da empresa sofreram com problemas técnicos e funcionaram com instabilidade. Veja:

Apagão na Microsoft : uma falha global nos serviços da Microsoft afetou empresas, governos e serviços de emergência em dezenas de países. O problema começou na quinta-feira (12) e persistiu até a sexta-feira (13), com falhas em ferramentas amplamente utilizadas no ambiente de trabalho, como o Outlook, o Teams e o assistente de inteligência artificial Copilot.

Um dia depois, todos os aeroportos dos Estados Unidos foram fechados. O motivo? Outra falha técnica, esta na comunicação entre os centros de comandos de tráfego aéreo no país. Foram mais de quatro horas sem pousos e decolagens em todo o país, o que interferiu na malha aérea mundial. Veja:

Apagão aéreo nos EUA : a paralisação de todos os aeroportos dos Estados Unidos , com pousos e decolagens interrompidos na sexta-feira (13), contribuiu para ampliar a teoria da conspiração. Uma falha no sistema de comunicação dos controladores de voo fez o país bloquear por mais de quatro horas o tráfego aéreo.

Passageiros aguardam no Aeroporto Internacional Logan, em East Boston, Massachusetts (EUA), após a Administração Federal de Aviação (FAA) dos EUA determinar uma paralisação nacional das decolagens "devido a circunstâncias extraordinárias e por motivos de segurança". A medida ocorreu após a agência relatar, anteriormente, graves problemas nas comunicações de controle de tráfego aéreo. — Foto: Brian Snyder/Reuters

Enquanto o fim de semana serviu para normalizar tanto os serviços de Microsoft quanto de tráfego aéreo nos EUA, a segunda-feira (16) registrou outros dois problemas: dificuldades de clientes em usar os serviços online de bancos americanos e, novamente, com aviões -- em falha na United Airlines. Veja:

Falhas com bancos: grandes bancos, também dos Estados Unidos, registraram problemas nesta segunda-feira (16). Milhares de clientes relataram dificuldades para acessar contas bancárias pela internet após um problema técnico em uma instituição financeira provocar um efeito cascata no sistema americano.

Problemas generalizados em companhia aérea: também nesta segunda, a United Airlines enfrentou uma falha em seus sistemas que provocou atrasos em alguns voos . Segundo a companhia, o problema foi resolvido em poucas horas. Após a solução, a companhia esclareceu que não havia indícios de ciberataque.

Falha em serviço bancário nos EUA — Foto: LM Otero / AP Photo/LM Otero

O tão esperado dia do apagão mundial não entregou o que a teoria conspiratória dizia. Porém, houve mais uma falha técnica nos Estados Unidos, desta vez na rede ultrassecreta de comunicações de segurança nacional, que ficou fora do ar; e um ataque hacker a mais de 200 sites. Veja:

Falha na segurança nacional dos EUA: uma interrupção afetou a comunicação interna da Agência de Segurança Nacional dos Estados Unidos (NSA, na sigla em inglês) , que, no entanto, ressaltou que suas "capacidades essenciais para o cumprimento de suas missões" permaneceram totalmente operacionais enquanto o problema ocorreu. O sistema, chamado NSA Net, permite que funcionários da agência compartilhem informações classificadas como confidenciais.

Ataque hacker a quase 200 sites: o ataque hacker envolveu sites como a BBC, o IKEA, e a Air France e atingiu cerca de 178 páginas, segundo o site especializado Cybernews. Segundo a agência AFP, o objetivo era roubar números de cartões de crédito e informações sobre criptomoedas dos usuários, além de instalar código malicioso em dispositivos da Apple.

articles.title: Husky Pandora: Justiça ordena que ONG de Cravinhos devolva cadela | G1
articles.standfirst: Carla afirma que Pandora foi anunciada como adotada um dia após fugir de casa. Associação diz que vai se manifestar quando conhecer a ação.
articles.summary: Após a husky Pandora ser doada por uma ONG de Cravinhos um dia após fugir, a Justiça determinou a devolução do animal à tutora Carla Martins sob pena de multa diária.
articles.body:
Justiça determina que husky doada por ONG após fugir retorne à família — Foto: Reprodução/Arquivo Pessoal

A tutora Carla Martins Ribeiro Tena, de Cravinhos (SP), diz que ouviu de uma funcionária da ONG que recolheu sua husky Pandora que só teria a cadela de volta “na frente do juiz” . Segundo ela, a Associação Ambientalista Toda Vida informou que entregou o animal a outra família um dia depois da fuga, em setembro.

Como mostrou o g1 , a Justiça determinou em 4 de novembro que a associação devolva Pandora em até 48 horas a partir da intimação, sob multa de R$ 500 por dia. A ONG afirma que ainda não recebeu notificação.

Ao g1 , Carla contou como foram os dias depois da fuga e a conversa com a entidade.

“Eu tava indignada como é que uma ONG que é pra cuidar dos animais faz isso”, diz.

Procurada, a associação afirmou por e-mail, nesta terça-feira (17), que não tem conhecimento da ação judicial e que vai se manifestar quando tiver acesso ao teor do processo e da decisão. A entidade não respondeu onde está a cadela.

Pandora tem 5 anos e vive com a família desde filhote. Carla reconhece que a cadela já tinha fugido de casa antes.

“Não é a primeira vez que ela foge. Isso a gente tem ciência”, afirma.

Segundo a tutora, Pandora escapou em uma quarta-feira. A família esperou cerca de duas horas pela volta dela, como costumava acontecer. Como a cadela não apareceu, o marido de Carla divulgou o desaparecimento no WhatsApp.

Foi uma cunhada quem encontrou a publicação da associação. Segundo Carla, a ONG divulgou nas redes sociais, na quinta-feira, que tinha encontrado a cadela e, no mesmo dia, informou que ela já tinha sido adotada.

“Isso foi o que a ONG me falou, que passou a cachorra para outra família”, conta.

ONG publicou sobre husky nas redes sociais no início de setembro — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

Carla diz que ligou para a associação cerca de uma semana depois da fuga. Segundo ela, a funcionária que atendeu, cujo nome ela não lembra, se recusou a informar quem tinha ficado com Pandora.

A tutora argumenta que a entidade deveria ter procurado os donos antes de encaminhar a cadela para adoção. “Você tem que ver se o cachorro tem dono primeiro”, diz.

Carla relata que, durante a conversa, a funcionária afirmou que a cadela tinha sido encontrada na rua e que ninguém tinha ido à casa da família para roubá-la. A tutora conta que subiu o tom.

“Eu vou pegar meu cachorro de volta sim, ele é meu cachorro”, diz ter respondido.

Segundo ela, a funcionária disse em seguida que a família só conseguiria a cadela “na frente do juiz”. Foi aí que Carla procurou advogados.

Carla conta que Pandora foi criada mais solta e é conhecida na vizinhança. A tutora diz que pretende colocar um rastreador na cadela quando ela voltar para casa.

“Eu vou colocar um chip nela, porque aí, se ela fugir, eu consigo ver onde ela tá, eu vou de carro e pego”, afirma.

Ela diz que receberia a ONG em casa se a entidade quisesse alertá-la sobre as fugas ou orientá-la.

“Eu ia receber de bom grado eles na minha casa, pra dar uma ideia pra mim, o que eu poderia fazer, entendeu? Não tem problema nenhum eu abrir a porta da minha casa”, diz.

Enquanto espera o oficial de Justiça, a tutora conta que a outra cachorra da família sente falta de Pandora e não quer mais ficar do lado de fora. Carla também diz ter medo de não reencontrar a husky.

articles.title: Planeta Atlântida 2027: Armandinho celebra 18ª participação | G1
articles.standfirst: Recordista de participações no festival, o músico chega à sua 18ª edição. Evento acontece nos dias 29 e 30 de janeiro, na Saba, em Xangri-lá.
articles.summary: Inspirando o lema do Planeta Atlântida 2027, Armandinho celebra o recorde de 18 participações no festival e compartilha planos de priorizar a família aos 56 anos.
articles.body:
Quando pisou pela primeira vez no palco do Planeta Atlântida, em 2003, Armandinho não sabia se aquele seria um capítulo duradouro ou apenas um instante marcante da carreira . Décadas depois, a resposta parece ter vindo em forma de homenagem.

Recordista de participações no festival, o cantor é o rosto da campanha da edição de 2027 com a frase "Pra sempre ou só por um momento" , inspirada em um trecho da música "Outra Noite Que Se Vai".

"Fico muito lisonjeado, muito feliz de fazer parte desse palco. E, na verdade, esse palco também faz parte de mim, e conta toda uma história e uma trajetória de uma vida e de uma carreira", resume.

Para Armandinho, o conceito do Planeta Atlântida 2027 dialoga diretamente com a experiência de quem frequenta o evento .

Ele acredita que cada pessoa guarda uma lembrança diferente do festival :

"Pessoas que se emocionam, que assistem a artistas, que sonham, pessoas que se conhecem, pessoas que começam uma relação no Planeta Atlântida, pessoas que retornam depois de muito tempo", observa. "Cada planeta é pra sempre ou só por um momento na vida deles também".

Agora, o cantor chega à 18ª edição no palco que o recebe de braços abertos. Depois de tanto tempo, a relação com o evento se mistura à própria trajetória. Do frio na barriga da estreia, quando não sabia se voltaria no ano seguinte, à homenagem que receberá nesta edição, ele vê no festival um retrato de sua carreira.

"A gente não sabia se no ano que vem ia estar presente, então tinha que aproveitar ao máximo aquele momento."

Ao longo dos anos, Armandinho viu o evento mudar de tamanho, de público e de geração . Também mudou de lugar dentro dele.

Se antes observava o festival da plateia, hoje se vê como alguém que ajuda a dar as boas-vindas ao público logo nas primeiras horas de festa.

Tradicionalmente escalado para tocar no fim da tarde , entre o pôr do sol e o início da noite, o cantor diz que passou a enxergar o próprio papel como o de alguém que recebe os planetários:

"Acabei me sentindo como anfitrião pelo fato de ser gaúcho. Acabei me sentindo o anfitrião de todo o festival, de estar preparando o terreno para as outras bandas virem. Principalmente, de trazer o público mais cedo para começar a festa mais cedo", diz.

Segundo ele, tocar no Planeta significa se apresentar não apenas para os próprios fãs, mas também para pessoas que foram assistir a outros artistas e acabam descobrindo suas músicas pelo caminho.

"Estou subindo no palco e tocando para o amor de outros artistas também. Quero conquistar essas pessoas novas que estão ali, quero mostrar o meu trabalho. Acho que é um jogo de sedução e de conquista", explica.

Armandinho no Planeta Atlântida em 2003 — Foto: Dulce Helfer/ Agencia RBS

Ao lembrar das primeiras edições que frequentou, Armandinho descreve um mundo bem diferente do que existe hoje. O cantor recorda que sua geração viveu o festival em uma época anterior às redes sociais e à cultura dos celulares apontados para todos os momentos.

Na lembrança dele, os encontros eram mais espontâneos . As histórias ficavam restritas a quem as viveu. O que acontecia raramente ultrapassava os limites do evento.

Foi uma fase, segundo ele, marcada pela ausência de filtros e por uma rebeldia que dificilmente encontraria espaço no cenário atual .

"Era uma geração mais livre. Uma geração que não tinha esse compromisso de ter que estar gravando, de ter que estar filmando ou documentando, uma geração que não se dispersava com o celular na mão", relembra.

Do palco, o músico observava amizades surgindo, romances começando e grupos vindos de diferentes regiões do estado se encontrando em torno da música.

"Foi uma experiência que tive com a minha geração de uma transformação muito grande na forma de como viver, principalmente de comunicação".

Armandinho sobe ao palco no Planeta Atlântida 2026 — Foto: Nani ArtClub

Se o Planeta mudou junto com as gerações, Armandinho acredita que suas canções também seguiram esse caminho.

Depois de 25 anos de carreira, o cantor, frequentemente chamado pelos fãs de " o poeta " pelas letras que falam de amor, liberdade e natureza, afirma ter a sensação de que deixou de ser o dono das próprias canções.

"Acho que eu não sou mais dono do meu repertório, as músicas não me pertencem mais, elas pertencem ao meu público. [...] Isso acaba mudando a forma de como se tocar e apresentar as músicas", reflete.

A ideia surge especialmente quando percebe como o repertório foi ganhando novos significados ao longo do tempo e acompanhando mudanças em sua banda, em seus shows e no próprio público.

Ele admite que não consegue medir o tamanho da influência que exerceu nesses anos , mas acredita que suas canções ajudaram a transmitir mensagens que considera fundamentais: respeito nas relações, autonomia para amar e valorização da natureza .

"Uma mensagem de amor livre, sem preconceito", resume.

Apesar de não pensar em aposentadoria, Armandinho afirma que vive uma nova fase .

Aos 56 anos, pretende reduzir a quantidade de apresentações para dedicar mais tempo à família. O nascimento da filha mais nova há quase dois anos teve peso importante nessa decisão.

O cantor conta que a rotina intensa de shows o afastou de muitos momentos da infância das filhas mais velhas e que agora deseja participar mais de perto do crescimento do bebê.

"Minha prioridade hoje é a família", diz.

Isso não significa abandonar a música . Os planos incluem novos projetos, entre eles a gravação de um show acústico em formato de luau, pensado para espaços ao ar livre e apresentações mais intimistas.

Armandinho no Planeta Atlântida 2026 — Foto: Duda Fortes/ Grupo RBS

Apontado pelas investigações como responsável por um esquema bilionário de sonegação de impostos, o empresário Ricardo Magro está foragido desde maio . Dono da Refinaria de Manguinhos (Refit), no Rio de Janeiro, ele é alvo de investigações que apuram fraudes tributárias cometidas ao longo de quase 20 anos.

Segundo dados da Procuradoria-Geral da Fazenda Nacional (PGFN) citados pelo Fantástico, o grupo de empresas ligado ao empresário acumula um rombo de mais de R$ 50 bilhões em impostos não pagos. Só a Refit deve R$ 27,6 bilhões, dos quais R$ 3 bilhões correspondem a tributos federais, mais de R$ 14 bilhões ao estado do Rio de Janeiro e R$ 10 bilhões ao estado de São Paulo.

O Ministério Público afirma que o dinheiro que deveria ter sido usado para o pagamento de tributos ajudou a construir um patrimônio bilionário. Ricardo Magro e outras 18 pessoas foram denunciados.

Uma das frentes de investigação revelou como o grupo conseguia reduzir drasticamente o pagamento de impostos na operação com combustíveis.

Em uma das operações contra Magro, a Agência Nacional do Petróleo (ANP) e a Receita Federal apreenderam quatro navios e identificaram que a Refit era, segundo a investigação, uma “refinaria que não refinava nada”.

As investigações apontaram que empresas sediadas nos Estados Unidos compravam gasolina, diesel e nafta já prontos para o consumo em diferentes partes do mundo. Quando as cargas eram enviadas ao Brasil, no entanto, os produtos eram declarados como se fossem petróleo bruto.

Segundo a investigação, notas fiscais eram fraudadas para modificar tanto a descrição dos produtos quanto a origem das cargas. Dessa forma, o grupo conseguia pagar menos impostos e aproveitar benefícios fiscais.

Em um dos navios investigados, uma carga declarada em R$ 142 milhões teria permitido à empresa deixar de pagar R$ 138 milhões em impostos. A mesma fraude, segundo a investigação, foi identificada nos outros três navios apreendidos.

“Do porto ao posto, sem imposto”, resumiu um dos entrevistados pelo Fantástico ao explicar a lógica atribuída ao esquema.

Dinheiro saía e retornava como investimento

A investigação também aponta um mecanismo para fazer o dinheiro circular entre diferentes empresas.

Segundo os investigadores, recursos eram enviados ao exterior, passavam por outras companhias e depois retornavam ao Brasil como se fossem investimentos de empresas americanas ou instaladas em paraísos fiscais.

O Ministério Público afirma que Magro estava nos dois lados das operações: empresas ligadas a ele nos Estados Unidos vendiam os produtos para empresas também ligadas ao empresário no Brasil.

Com o avanço das apurações, os investigadores identificaram uma estrutura ainda maior. Segundo o MP, operadores financeiros criaram ou administraram 192 empresas e 25 fundos de investimento, por onde circulava dinheiro arrecadado com as fraudes.

Os investigadores afirmam ainda que, ao longo do tempo, Magro deixou de aparecer formalmente no controle de diversas empresas. Familiares teriam passado a figurar nos negócios, enquanto o empresário continuaria usufruindo do patrimônio.

As investigações contra Ricardo Magro avançaram em diferentes frentes. De acordo com o Fantástico, o empresário foi alvo de seis operações em um período de um ano.

Em uma das ações mais recentes, o Ministério Público do Rio mirou 14 pessoas e atingiu também o núcleo familiar do empresário. A Justiça decretou as prisões do tio Ernesto dos Santos Andrade, do avô Manoel Joaquim Andrade, do pai João Manoel Magro e da mãe Gabriela Andrade Magro.

Ernesto e Manoel Joaquim foram presos em São Paulo. Como os pais de Magro moram em Portugal, o cumprimento dos mandados depende de cooperação internacional.

O piloto da Copa Truck André Marques também foi preso. Segundo o Ministério Público, os investigados atuavam como operadores financeiros do esquema.

Outro nome apontado pela investigação é Cristiano Beraldo, ex-funcionário da Refit. Segundo o MP, ele trabalhou na empresa entre 2015 e 2019 e era considerado os “olhos, braços, mãos e pés” de Magro. Após um período de rompimento entre os dois, Beraldo teria se tornado operador do esquema no exterior.

Em agosto, a Justiça do Rio decretou a falência da Refit.

A dívida tributária atribuída à empresa representa parte expressiva do rombo investigado. Dos mais de R$ 50 bilhões em impostos não pagos relacionados ao grupo, R$ 27,6 bilhões são atribuídos somente à refinaria, segundo os dados citados pelo Fantástico.

Para o Ministério Público, a dimensão da dívida contrasta com o patrimônio associado ao empresário e à família no exterior.

Ricardo Magro mora nos Estados Unidos há 11 anos e possui Green Card, documento que permite residência e trabalho no país.

Foragido desde maio, ele teve uma nova prisão pedida em outra investigação. Também foi solicitado que seu nome fosse incluído na difusão vermelha da Interpol, mecanismo utilizado para ajudar a localizar foragidos internacionais.

Segundo o Fantástico, o paradeiro de Magro permanece desconhecido pelas autoridades.

Em uma mensagem trocada entre dois investigados e obtida durante a apuração, ele é chamado de “mestre”. Um dos interlocutores escreve que “quem é mestre nisso é o chefe”, ao falar sobre sonegação.

Para os investigadores, o caso não envolve a falta de recursos para quitar os tributos, mas a decisão deliberada de não pagá-los apesar do patrimônio atribuído ao empresário.

“Nós não estamos falando de uma pessoa que não tem dinheiro para pagar imposto. A gente está falando de uma pessoa que escolhe não pagar imposto, apesar de ter um patrimônio bilionário nas suas contas”, afirma um dos responsáveis pela investigação ouvido pelo Fantástico.

articles.title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave
articles.summary: Europe hopes to be a leader in a new generation of computer chips which use light to process data.
articles.body:
"Photonic chips are on the verge of a breakthrough," says Ton van Mol of the Dutch research institute TNO.

If van Mol is right – and TNO, the European Union and the Dutch government are backing the idea with millions of euros - then the technology could be a gamechanger.

The chips which run today's society, from your phone and TV, to the vast data centres meeting our insatiable desire for AI, are mostly electrical.

They process data by shunting electrons around tiny circuits – a single microchip produced today can contain billions of transistors, and sizes are measured in nanometres (one nanometre is a billionth of a metre).

Because they use light instead of electricity, photonic chips are faster, use less energy and generate less heat than traditional computer chips.

Van Mol hopes for an acceleration in photonics similar to the one seen in electrical chips since the 1970s.

"With optical chips, you are now where electronic chips were maybe 40 [or] 50 years ago."

American, Taiwanese and Chinese firms dominate the computer chip industry, but Europe sees the emergence of photonic chips as a fresh opportunity to lead, on what could be, a key future technology.

Which is why the European Union has committed €400m ($450m; £330m) to a project called PIX Europe , with the stated goal of making the continent "a global leader in emerging technology for Photonic Integrated Chips".

"Europe said 'we need to have our own manufacturing in-house'," says van Mol, who is leading a key part of the programme.

"We cannot depend like in the past that everything is manufactured in the US or China - that's not wise, so the [European] Chips Act was called into life, and one of the parts of the act is to build pilot lines to really bring the technology, which is now in labs, to the next stage - manufacturing."

Electronic and photonic chips are produced on wafers made up of hundreds of individual chips. Factories with machines that can handle bigger wafers can churn out chips more efficiently.

"[Photonic chip] manufacturing worldwide is [currently] done on wafers which are four inches (10cm) in size, and the next step is to scale-up production to a six-inch wafer," says van Mol.

His team are already building a 10,000 sq m factory to produce six-inch indium phosphide wafers on the High Tech Campus in the Dutch city of Eindhoven.

It's due to fully open in 2030 and will be a major step forward, not just for photonics in Europe, but around the world, according to van Mol.

"That's the development TNO is going to do, in a pilot line which is really serious.

"In 2030, we hope that we have a stable, reproducible, high-yield process, and then the intention is that the pilot line [opens] to industrial parties who can make commercial production out of it."

Europe does have one crucial player in the current computer chip industry - ASML.

The Netherlands-based tech giant is the only company in the world able to build the machines needed to make the most sophisticated semiconductors.

Which is why ASML products will sit at the heart of the pilot line in Eindhoven - it's no coincidence that van Mol's project is based around the corner from ASML's headquarters.

"The way you produce these [photonic] chips is very similar to the way you produce electrical or electronic chip," says van Mol.

"You use the same type of equipment, you also need a high-end clean room, you also use wafers, so the production method is very similar to the traditional semiconductor technology."

ASML itself is keen to explore the opportunities that the emerging technology of photonics could offer.

"Europe has a strong position in photonics research. The next challenge is translating those innovations into industrial-scale manufacturing," says Stanislas Baron, who is the head of ASML's EU/US Customer Team.

ASML's unique success has helped build an influential and lucrative network of companies and institutions devoted to semiconductor technology in and around Eindhoven, and it's a model for what Europe is trying to achieve with photonic chips.

The Eindhoven project has the backing of former ASML chief executive Peter Wennink, author of an influential report for the Dutch government called The Roadmap to Future Prosperity , which noted that the market for photonics was expected to grow 10 to 20 times in the next 10 years.

In a news release backing the new pilot line, Wennink described it as "a launchpad for Europe's future digital economy".

"By investing in scalable production capacity, we are creating an ecosystem that can help shape the global technological direction," he said.

Of course, Europe is not alone in looking to the potential of photonics to earn a global economic advantage.

In June this year, US photonics company Coherent announced what it called "the world's first and largest volume-production six-inch indium phosphide manufacturing platform" at its plant in Sherman, in Texas.

The expansion is backed by chip manufacturing giant Nvidia, as well as $50 million public funds under the US Chips Act.

It's an illustration of how quickly the market is moving, and how central photonic chips could be to the continuing race to retain an influential stake in AI and technological development more generally.

Europe's bid to establish itself as a global leader in photonic chips – exemplified by the Eindhoven project – is the kind of strategy that makes sense in a globalised economy, says Joris Teer, policy analyst at the European Institute for Security Studies in Brussels.

If the continent can take a lead in photonic chips, then future developments in AI and data will partly be dependent on Europe.

"Europe knows that its high energy and labour costs, skilled workforce shortages, and lack of private and public capital make an across-the-board reindustrialisation strategy impossible", Teer says.

"To retain influence, ensuring dependence on European parties rather than European autonomy is key."

Once up and running, the Eindhoven project will provide a pilot production line which can be used multiple companies.

It will be open to businesses across Europe and beyond, who can design and build chips without having to develop their own expensive production facilities.

"What we want to establish here is what we call a foundry model; there's no intention to have our own product," Ton van Mol says.

Instead, they will produce to order for outside customers.

It's the same idea which, at huge scale, has brought Taiwanese-based giant TSMC a position of global dominance in the manufacture of microchips.

Photonic chips are already in use, in highly specialised areas in data centres and in Lidar (light detection and ranging) sensor technology, for instance.

For van Mol of TNO, helping the industry to scale up, by easing production challenges and increasing capacity, is the key step to moving them into the tech we use in our daily lives, like phones and laptops, and to drive innovation in areas like medical scanners and 6G communications.

"The demand is there", says van Mol, "and the end goal is to have, in Europe, manufacturing of these chips, which is strategically very important because these chips [could] become the backbone of all data and telecom."
